newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - European markets rise as turmoil subsides.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - European markets rise as turmoil subsides.

text.p: European markets rose strongly on Monday as bourses, bonds and the dollar got a boost from a deal over an EU stability pact and Wall Street began the week in buoyant mood.
An accord between European Union leaders in Dublin on a mechanism for ensuring monetary discipline after the launch of a single currency in 1999 boosted bond markets and the dollar.
That, in turn, helped stock markets recover ground after last week's volatility and Wall Street opened strongly following news of a merger between aerospace giants Boeing and McDonnell Douglas.
German stocks closed floor trade two percent higher, outpacing gains on Europe's other two biggest bourses -- London and Paris.

Investors remained wary after the recent market turmoil, however, and traders forecast the mood would remain cautious ahead of Tuesday's meeting of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee, which sets U.S. interest rates.
The dollar was firmer against a bruised mark in thin afternoon trade as global asset markets calmed and the German currency was undermined by the stability pact deal.

Analysts said the pact bolstered optimism that Europe's single currrency project would go ahead on time in 1999 and increased the chance of a broad-based economic and monetary union (EMU) that would include Italy and Spain.
It was also seen lowering Europe's interest rate horizon, thereby buoying the dollar and yen against European currencies.

"The renewed surge in EMU optimism was always likely to be negative for the mark and this has combined with steadier stock amd bond markets to give the dollar a new lift," said Peter Wood, currency trader at Bank of Boston in London.
By 1530 GMT the dollar was quoted around 1.5538 marks and 113.98 yen, compared with 1.5473 and 113.95 in late European business on Friday.

Government bond markets also gained on the news from Dublin. German bunds got an added boost from an unexpected dip in an influential German business confidence index, although they slipped a bit later.
The London, Paris and Frankfurt equity markets all shot higher at the start, but only Frankfurt managed to sustain the pace.
Germany's 30-share DAX index zoomed 56 points in floor trade, closing two percent up at 2,855.79. In later computerised trade, the IBIS DAX stood 22 points higher at 2,838.
"But volumes are still a bit thin. Investors are still holding back a bit. Some think there is still room for a correction down to 2,750," one Frankfurt trader said.
Industrial giant Daimler Benz AG, whose Dasa unit is one of the partners in the European Airbus aircraft-maker, fell earlier on news that McDonnell Douglas and Boeing were to merge.
The stock pulled back later to trade at 100.95, 2.15 marks up on the day, as initial fears of the impact to Airbus's business were seen as overdone.
Europe's biggest share market, London, traded well off its highest levels through the afternoon, tracking Wall Street in light volume.
Dealers said the Christmas holiday season had begun to dampen market enthusiasm, as had concerns that the Dow could still suffer a downward correction.

French stocks also slipped from their highest levels of the day -- reached after banks cut their base lending rates to 6.30 percent from 6.55. Earlier the Bank of France left its rates unchanged at the weekly tender.
By 1545 GMT the CAC-40 index was up 13.64 points, or 0.6 percent, at 2,217.05.
Michelin jumped 2.28 percent to 265 francs, having lost 4.45 percent last week on talk of a capital increase. "It's a rebound. Last week's losers are leading today," a trader said.
CURRENCIES AT 1545 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.5538 marks and 113.98 yen compared with 1.5473 and 113.95 in late business on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1545 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index of top British shares was up 9.9 points at 3,982.3.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was up 13.64 points, or 0.6 percent, at 2,217.05..
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX ended floor trade up 56.08 points at 2,855.79. In later screen-based trade, the IBIS DAX inded was 19.79 points at 2,835.56.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed barely lower at $368.25 against $368.60 in the morning and $369.00 on Friday afternoon. Silver was off one cent at $4.82.
